title: In vitro corrosion resistance of a Ta2O5 nanofilm on MAO coated magnesium alloy AZ31 by atomic layer deposition

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Mg alloy AZ31 corrodes fast in physiological solution. MAO coatings on Mg leave micropores and microcracks through which aggressive ions reach the substrate.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n1b (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n5 (DES/route), n6 (PRC/deposition), n7 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: The outer film is Ta-O bonded Ta2O5. Ta2O5 covers the MAO surface across the whole field.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (STR/chemistry/bonding), n10 (STR/microstructure/distribution), n11 (STR/microstructure/porosity). Premises: Reference binding energies: Ta2O5 Ta 4d/Ta 4f doublets, Ta-O O 1s near 530.6 eV

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: The sealing Ta2O5 film acts as a physical barrier that keeps aggressive ions away from the Mg substrate. Corrosion resistance in Hank's solution ranks MAO/Ta2O5 > MAO > AZ31, with corrosion current about 2.7 decades below MAO
states.detail: Absorbed: n16 (MEC/pathway), n12 (PRP/value). Premises: Ta2O5 is chemically stable and corrosion resistant in aqueous media; Lower corrosion current and higher low-frequency |Z| mean higher corrosion resistance

states.title: Performance state
states.head: Over 294 h in Hank's solution MAO/Ta2O5 keeps a low steady hydrogen evolution rate, while AZ31 and MAO rise after ~170 h. After 294 h in Hank's solution the MAO/Ta2O5 surface stays largely intact, while AZ31 and MAO crack and pit

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Sealing MAO-coated AZ31 with an ALD Ta2O5 nanofilm markedly improves its in-vitro corrosion resistance

nodes.title: ECHEM:potentiodynamic, F4, F5, F6
nodes.head: Polarization curves: corrosion current ranks MAO/Ta2O5 < MAO < AZ31, the MAO/Ta2O5 curve lying 2-3 decades left of MAO. |Z| at 0.01 Hz ranks MAO/Ta2O5 (~2e7) > MAO (~7e4) > AZ31 (~4e3 ohm cm2).
nodes.solves: Corrosion resistance in Hank's solution ranks MAO/Ta2O5 > MAO > AZ31, with corrosion current about 2.7 decades below MAO
nodes.op: compare across conditions, cross check consistency
nodes.note: Ecorr about -1.42 (AZ31), -1.70 (MAO), -1.44 V/SCE (MAO/Ta2O5), matching the text; MAO/Ta2O5 curve is noisy near Ecorr (1e-10 to 1e-9 A/cm2); text icorr 1.05e-6 -> 2.23e-9 A/cm2 (Table 1, not in packet) about 3.7 decades above AZ31 and 2.4 above MAO; text says three and two orders the ~2.7-decade icorr gap (F4) and 2.4-decade |Z| gap (F5a) between MAO and MAO/Ta2O5 are not matched by the early immersion rates
nodes.detail: o9: Polarization curves: corrosion current ranks MAO/Ta2O5 < MAO < AZ31, the MAO/Ta2O5 curve lying 2-3 decades left of MAO; o11: |Z| at 0.01 Hz ranks MAO/Ta2O5 (~2e7) > MAO (~7e4) > AZ31 (~4e3 ohm cm2); o13: In the first 50 h MAO/Ta2O5 evolves hydrogen only slightly less than MAO: peak ~0.005 vs ~0.0085, error bars overlapping, near-equal after 24 h
nodes.inner_audit: o13: the ~2.7-decade icorr gap (F4) and 2.4-decade |Z| gap (F5a) between MAO and MAO/Ta2O5 are not matched by the early immersion rates
